title: Two Neighbors Compare Notes on Staying Patient
script: Sri: [tired] Amir, honestly, this year has tested my patience more than any year I can remember.
Amir: I understand that more than you might think. My own year hasn't been easy either.
Sri: What happened to you? You always seem so calm at the mosque, greeting everyone with that same warm smile.
Amir: [quietly] I lost my job in January. I still haven't found steady work since then.
Sri: I had no idea. You never once complained about it, not even quietly.
Amir: [honestly] I do speak honestly with trusted people, but I try not to let anger control how I treat everyone around me.
Sri: That's a strong way to think. I wish I could manage my own stress that calmly.
Amir: [worried] It isn't calm every single day, believe me. Some nights I lie awake, worried and frustrated about money.
Sri: What do you do on those nights?
Amir: [steadily] I pray, continue applying for work, and ask for help when I need it. I do not know when the hardship will end.
Sri: [overwhelmed] I've been struggling with my mother's illness this year, and some days I feel close to breaking completely.
Amir: I noticed you visiting the hospital often. I never asked, because I didn't want to intrude on something private.
Sri: [grateful] I appreciate that, actually. Some people ask too many questions, and it becomes exhausting to keep answering them.
Amir: For what it's worth, I've seen how patiently you handle her appointments, even while working full time.
Sri: Some days patience feels impossible. I snap at small things that don't even matter.
Amir: [regretful] Struggle is human. We can apologize after a sharp moment and return to patient action again.
Sri: I like that. I always thought righteous people simply never got tired or frustrated at all.
Amir: No one is like that, honestly. We just keep quietly trying, and hope that Allah rewards sincere effort.
Sri: [peacefully] Talking with you today actually helped more than you probably realize, Amir.
Amir: It helped me too, Sri. Sometimes we forget everyone around us is carrying something heavy too.

quiz.question: What happened to Amir in January?
quiz.explanation: Amir explains he lost his job in January and still hasn't found steady work.

quiz.question: Why does Amir say complaining doesn't help?
options: It is against his religion to speak
It only makes the waiting feel heavier for everyone
quiz.explanation: Amir says complaining only makes the waiting feel heavier for himself and everyone around him.

quiz.question: What has Sri been struggling with this year?
quiz.explanation: Sri says she has been struggling with her mother's illness this year.

quiz.question: Why did Amir never ask Sri about her hospital visits?
options: He didn't want to intrude on something private
quiz.explanation: Amir noticed her visiting often but never asked because he didn't want to intrude on something private.

quiz.question: According to Amir, what is righteousness really about?
options: Returning to patience again after we fail at it
quiz.explanation: Amir says righteousness isn't about never struggling, it's about returning to patience again after failing at it.

quiz.question: What wrong idea did Sri have about righteous people?
options: They always work at a hospital
They never feel tired or frustrated
quiz.explanation: Amir explains that good people still struggle and keep trying.

quiz.question: Does Amir hide every difficult feeling?
options: No, he speaks with trusted people
No, he tells the whole mosque
quiz.explanation: The revised script allows honest, safe support.

quiz.question: What actions does Amir take?
options: He prays, applies, and asks for help
quiz.explanation: His patience includes both faith and practical effort.

quiz.question: Why did Amir not question Sri earlier?
options: He did not see her hospital visits
He wanted to respect her privacy
quiz.explanation: He noticed her situation without demanding information.

quiz.question: What can Sri do after speaking sharply?
quiz.explanation: A difficult moment does not prevent a better next action.
